- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model forecasts a sharp upward move after a recent dip, check for lag: true price often reverses within 3–5 days; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and model forecasts a decline, often overshoots; cap downward forecasts at 1–2% below recent low if sentiment remains negative.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if model forecasts > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–3% downward correction in middle of forecast window.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks > 15% above recent high, reduce by 10–15% in next 3–5 days unless sentiment remains bullish.
- Sentiment history with high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00) suggests model overfits; apply smoothing: average last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast weight.
